title: Poisoning Basics: Routes, Toxidromes and the PCP Approach
next: Chapter 36, Lesson 2: Alcohol, stimulants, sedatives and opioids, with naloxone

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already keep the scene safe, manage the airway, check the glucose and give naloxone. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Sort a poisoning by type and route, and spot a dangerous scene
  2. Use toxidromes to reason from signs to a drug class
  3. Take a sharper history, and know what the PCP adds for the unknown overdose

Textbook: Chapter 36, PDF pages 3094–3126
slides.say: Welcome to toxicology, the study of poisons, which we'll cover in three lessons. As EMRs, you already know a lot: keep the scene safe, manage the airway, ventilate with a bag-valve mask, check the blood glucose, and give naloxone. As a PCP, you need to think more like a detective. Today we'll cover three things. First, how poisonings happen and how poisons get in, because the route tells you whether the scene itself is dangerous. Second, toxidromes, which are patterns of signs that point to a drug class. Third, a sharper history, and what the PCP adds for a patient with a decreased level of consciousness and no clear cause.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎进入毒理学，也就是研究毒物的学科，我们分三节课讲。作为 EMR，你们已经会很多：确保现场安全、管理气道、用球囊面罩通气、测血糖、给纳洛酮。作为 PCP，你要更像侦探一样思考。今天讲三件事：第一，中毒是怎么发生的、毒物怎么进入身体，因为途径决定现场本身危不危险；第二，中毒综合征，也就是指向某一类药物的一组体征；第三，更精准的病史询问，以及对原因不明、意识水平下降的病人，PCP 多做什么。

slides.title: Intentional or unintentional?
slides.body:
• Adults: poisoning is often intentional, and often serious
  • Canada 2017: 4,392 poisoning deaths, 4,108 from drug overdose
  • Drug deaths: 5.8 → 11.9 per 100,000 (2011 → 2019), mainly fentanyl
  • Unintentional: dosing errors, unusual reactions, a dose taken twice
  • Children under 5: pain relievers and cleaners top the list
slides.say: Poisonings fall into two groups: intentional and unintentional. In adults they're often intentional, and suicide attempts commonly use drugs, so take every adult poisoning seriously. The numbers show why. In Canada in two thousand seventeen, there were four thousand three hundred ninety-two poisoning deaths, and four thousand one hundred eight were drug overdoses. The death rate doubled between two thousand eleven and two thousand nineteen, mostly from fentanyl and similar opioids. Unintentional poisonings include dosing errors, unusual individual reactions, and an older person who forgets a dose and takes it again. In children under five, the most common exposures are pain relievers and cleaning products, and pills can look like candy.
slides.sayZh: 中毒分两类：故意和无意。成人中毒常是故意的，自杀常用药物，所以每个成人中毒都要认真对待。数字说明了原因：二零一七年加拿大有四千三百九十二人死于中毒，其中四千一百零八人是药物过量。二零一一到二零一九年间死亡率翻了一倍，主要是芬太尼及类似阿片类。无意中毒包括给药错误、个体的特异反应，以及老人忘了已经吃过药又吃一次。五岁以下儿童最常见的是止痛药和清洁剂，药片看起来很像糖果。

slides.title: The Poison Centre: an expert on call
slides.body:
BC Drug and Poison Centre: 1-800-567-8911

  • Specially trained nurses and pharmacists, 24/7
  • They advise registered health professionals, like you
  • Advice you can act on, not messages for the hospital
  • Your call also feeds regional poisoning data

Record every finding, even if you don't know what it means.
slides.say: No one can memorize every drug and chemical, so use the experts. B.C.'s Drug and Poison Centre is staffed twenty-four hours a day by specially trained nurses and pharmacists. They can advise registered health professionals, and that includes you. Their advice is practical, things you can act on yourself, like which symptoms to prepare for. They won't give you a message to pass on to the hospital. Your call also helps them track poisoning trends in the region. Here's a good PCP habit: write down every finding, even if you don't know what it means. Someone at the Poison Centre probably will.
slides.sayZh: 没有人能记住所有药物和化学品，所以要用专家。BC 药物与中毒中心二十四小时由受过专门训练的护士和药剂师值守。他们可以给注册医护人员提供建议，你也包括在内。他们的建议很实用，是你自己能执行的，比如该准备应对哪些症状；他们不会让你给医院转话。你的来电也帮助他们追踪本地区的中毒趋势。一个好的 PCP 习惯：每个发现都记下来，哪怕你不知道它的意义，中毒中心的人很可能知道。

slides.title: Four ways in
slides.body:
RouteExampleKey point
Ingestionpills, cleaners, plantsmost common; mostly absorbed in the small intestine
InhalationCO, chlorine, fumesfastest onset; rescuers at risk
InjectionIV drugs, bites, stingsinto a vessel = immediate effect
Absorptionorganophosphates, solventsmay need decontamination
slides.say: Poisons get in four ways. Ingestion, or swallowing, is the most common, usually medicines or cleaning products at home. Little is absorbed in the stomach; most is absorbed in the small intestine, so there's a window of time. Inhalation is the fastest: gases reach the alveoli and enter the blood almost at once, and anyone still in that air keeps breathing it, including you. Injection includes IV drug use and bites or stings; a dose that goes straight into a vessel acts immediately. Absorption through the skin matters most with organophosphate pesticides and solvents. As a PCP, the route shapes your scene plan, because inhaled and absorbed poisons can hurt the crew.
slides.sayZh: 毒物有四种进入途径。食入最常见，通常是家里的药物或清洁剂；胃吸收很少，主要在小肠吸收，所以有一段时间窗。吸入最快：气体到达肺泡几乎立刻入血，任何还待在那片空气里的人都会继续吸入，包括你。注射包括静脉吸毒和叮咬蜇伤；直接打进血管的剂量会立即起效。经皮吸收在有机磷农药和溶剂中最重要。作为 PCP，途径决定你的现场计划，因为吸入和经皮的毒物会伤到救援人员。

slides.title: When the scene is the poison
slides.body:
• Several patients, same place, no mechanism → think toxic gas
  • Confined spaces and industrial sites: extra caution
  • Many gases have no colour or smell
  • No entry without proper breathing protection
  • Chemical on skin or clothes: decontaminate before loading
  • Overdose patients can be violent: call police early
slides.say: Here's where the scene becomes the danger. If you find several people in the same place with medical complaints and no clear mechanism, think toxic gas until proven otherwise, especially in a confined space or an industrial site. Many dangerous gases have no colour and no smell, so you get no warning. Don't go in without the right breathing protection; let equipped teams remove the patients. If the skin or clothing is soaked with a chemical like an organophosphate pesticide, the patient needs decontamination before entering your ambulance, often with a hazmat team. And some overdose patients are agitated or violent, so calling police or a crisis team early is part of good scene management.
slides.sayZh: 这时候现场本身就是危险。如果同一地点有好几个人出现内科症状、又没有明显的受伤机制，在排除之前都要当作有毒气体，尤其是在密闭空间或工业现场。很多危险气体无色无味，不会给你任何预警。没有合适的呼吸防护不要进去，让有装备的队伍把病人移出来。如果皮肤或衣服浸透了化学品，比如有机磷农药，病人上救护车前要先洗消，通常要和危险品小组配合。有些过量的病人会激动甚至暴力，及早叫警察或危机小组也是现场管理的一部分。

slides.q: You arrive at a farm workshop. Two workers inside are confused, and one is vomiting. There is no sign of trauma. What is your best first action?
options: Run in and drag them out quickly before you assess
Stay outside, suspect a toxic gas, and call for equipped help to remove them
Go in and check their SpO₂ to rule out a gas
Give naloxone to both workers right away
slides.say: Let's check your scene sense. You arrive at a farm workshop. Two workers inside are confused, and one is vomiting. There's no sign of trauma. What's your best first action? A, run in and drag them out quickly before you assess. B, stay outside, suspect a toxic gas, and call for equipped help to remove them. C, go in and check their oxygen saturation to rule out a gas. D, give naloxone to both workers right away. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 考考你的现场意识。你到达一个农场工作间，里面两名工人意识混乱，其中一人在呕吐，没有外伤迹象。最好的第一步是什么？A 冲进去迅速把他们拖出来再评估；B 留在外面，怀疑有毒气体，呼叫有装备的人员把他们移出来；C 进去测血氧来排除气体中毒；D 立刻给两人都用纳洛酮。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Several patients in one place with medical complaints and no mechanism means a possible toxic gas, and many gases give no warning. Running in, A, can make you the next patient. A normal saturation, C, doesn't rule out a gas; in carbon monoxide poisoning the pulse oximeter can read normal, and you'd still be inside breathing it. Naloxone, D, treats opioid breathing problems, and nothing here points to opioids.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。同一地点多名病人出现内科症状、没有受伤机制，就可能是有毒气体，而很多气体毫无预警。A 冲进去，你可能成为下一个病人。C 血氧正常也排除不了气体中毒：一氧化碳中毒时血氧仪可以显示正常，而你还在里面吸着气体。D 纳洛酮治疗的是阿片类引起的呼吸问题，这里没有任何指向阿片类的线索。

slides.title: Toxidromes: patterns, not poisons
slides.body:
ToxidromeLook for
Opioidpinpoint pupils, slow breathing, drowsy to coma
Cholinergicwet: DUMBELS, small pupils, weakness
Anticholinergicdry, hot, red skin; big pupils; fast pulse; delirium
Stimulanthigh BP, fast pulse, big pupils, agitation, fever
Sedative-hypnoticdrowsy, slurred, unsteady, slow breathing
slides.say: There are thousands of poisons, but far fewer patterns. A toxidrome is the group of signs a class of poisons causes. Opioids give pinpoint pupils, slow breathing and drowsiness. Cholinergic poisons, like organophosphate pesticides, make the patient wet: drooling, tears, vomiting, diarrhea, and small pupils. Anticholinergic drugs, like some antihistamines and older antidepressants, do the opposite: dry, hot, red skin, big pupils, a fast pulse and delirium. Stimulants, also called sympathomimetics, raise the blood pressure and heart rate, widen the pupils, and cause agitation and fever. Sedative-hypnotics cause drowsiness, slurred speech, poor balance and slow breathing. As a PCP, match the pattern first, then confirm it with the history.
slides.sayZh: 毒物成千上万，但模式少得多。中毒综合征就是一类毒物引起的一组体征。阿片类：针尖样瞳孔、呼吸慢、嗜睡。胆碱能毒物，比如有机磷农药，让病人「湿」：流口水、流泪、呕吐、腹泻、瞳孔缩小。抗胆碱能药物，比如部分抗组胺药和老式抗抑郁药，正好相反：皮肤干、热、红，瞳孔散大，脉搏快，谵妄。兴奋剂（也叫拟交感药）使血压和心率升高、瞳孔散大，引起激越和发热。镇静催眠药引起嗜睡、口齿不清、站不稳和呼吸慢。作为 PCP，先对模式，再用病史确认。

slides.title: Quick clues: pupils, skin, smell
slides.body:
Pupilssmall: opioids, organophosphateslarge: stimulants, atropine, CO, cyanide
Skinwet: cholinergic, stimulantsdry and hot: anticholinergic
Smellbitter almond: cyanidegarlic: organophosphates

DUMBELS: Diarrhea, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia / Bronchospasm / Bronchorrhea, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation
slides.say: Three quick checks help you pick the toxidrome. Pupils: small pupils suggest opioids or organophosphates; large pupils suggest stimulants, atropine-like drugs, carbon monoxide or cyanide. Skin: stimulants and cholinergic poisons make the skin wet, while anticholinergic drugs make it dry and hot. That's the easiest way to tell a stimulant from an anticholinergic, since both cause a fast pulse and big pupils. Smell: bitter almonds suggest cyanide, and garlic suggests organophosphates. For the wet cholinergic patient, remember DUMBELS: diarrhea, urination, miosis, which means small pupils, bradycardia and bronchial secretions, emesis, lacrimation, which means tears, and salivation.
slides.sayZh: 三个快速检查帮你判断中毒综合征。瞳孔：缩小提示阿片类或有机磷；散大提示兴奋剂、阿托品类药物、一氧化碳或氰化物。皮肤：兴奋剂和胆碱能毒物让皮肤湿，抗胆碱能药让皮肤干热；这是区分兴奋剂和抗胆碱能最简单的方法，因为两者都会心率快、瞳孔大。气味：苦杏仁味提示氰化物，大蒜味提示有机磷。对「湿」的胆碱能病人，记住 DUMBELS：腹泻、排尿、缩瞳（瞳孔小）、心动过缓和支气管分泌物增多、呕吐、流泪、流涎。

slides.title: Tolerance, dependence, withdrawal
slides.body:
Toleranceneeds more for the same effect
Dependencephysical: withdrawal when stoppedpsychological: craving
Withdrawalpredictable signs after stoppingcan be dangerous
  • Potentiation: one drug boosts another
  • Synergism: together worse than the sum
  • Designer drugs: fentanyl analogues hundreds to thousands of times stronger
slides.say: Substance use has its own vocabulary, and you'll need it on the COPR exam. Tolerance means the person needs a bigger dose for the same effect. Physical dependence means the body has adapted, so stopping the drug causes withdrawal, a predictable set of signs. Psychological dependence is the craving for the good feeling. Potentiation is when one drug boosts another, and synergism is when two drugs together do more than the sum of their effects, like alcohol with sedatives. Designer drugs are small chemical changes to existing drugs; illegal labs now make fentanyl analogues hundreds or thousands of times stronger than fentanyl. That matters for naloxone, as you'll see next lesson.
slides.sayZh: 物质使用有自己的一套术语，COPR 考试会用到。耐受是指需要更大剂量才能达到同样效果。生理依赖是指身体已经适应，停药就会出现戒断，也就是一组可预测的症状。心理依赖是对那种舒服感觉的渴求。增效作用是一种药放大另一种药的效果；协同作用是两种药合在一起的效果大于各自之和，比如酒精加镇静药。设计师药物是对已有药物做小的化学改动；现在非法实验室造出的芬太尼类似物比芬太尼强几百到几千倍。这对纳洛酮很重要，下节课会讲到。

slides.title: The PCP history: six questions
slides.body:
1. What? Bring bottles, pills, containers, plant parts
  2. When? Stomach binding drops fast after 30–60 min
  3. How much? Count pills left; street "hits" = doses
  4. What else? Often several drugs, often alcohol
  5. Vomited? When, how much, any pills in it?
  6. Why? Record it in the patient's own words
slides.say: As a PCP, your history drives the hospital's next steps, so ask six questions. What was taken? Bring the bottles, the remaining pills, closed product containers, or a sample of the plant. When? The chance of binding the poison in the stomach drops fast after the first thirty to sixty minutes. How much? Have someone count the pills left to estimate the most that could have been taken; street drugs come in hits, so three hits means three doses. What else? Most intentional overdoses involve more than one drug, often alcohol. Has the patient vomited? And why? Don't assume they wanted to get high. Put their words in quotation marks on your report.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你的病史决定医院的下一步，所以要问六个问题。吃了什么？把药瓶、剩下的药片、封好的产品容器或植物样本带上。什么时候？过了最初三十到六十分钟，在胃里结合毒物的机会就迅速下降。吃了多少？请人数一数剩下的药片，估算最多可能吃了多少；街头毒品按「hit」计，三个 hit 就是三倍剂量。还用了什么？大多数故意过量都不止一种药，常有酒精。有没有呕吐？为什么用？别假设他只是想嗨，把病人的原话加引号写进报告。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: decreased LOC, cause unknown
slides.body:
BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol: also covers decreased LOC with no known cause

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway: position, suction, adjuncts
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%; lateral position if needed
  • Vitals with BGL; check for stroke
  • BGL < 4.0, protects airway → oral glucose
  • EMR: can't protect airway → glucagon

PCP adds

  • Vascular access
  • Confirmed low BGL → D10W 10–25 g
  • Glucagon only if no IV
  • Transport after the first dose
slides.say: Many poisoned patients arrive with a decreased level of consciousness and no clear cause. In BC, the Diabetic Emergencies protocol also covers a decreased LOC with no known cause, so it's your safety net. Every licence level manages the airway with positioning, suction and adjuncts, gives oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, uses the side position if needed, and takes vital signs including a blood glucose, plus a stroke check. If the glucose is under four point zero and the patient can protect the airway, give oral glucose; at EMR level, if they can't, give glucagon. The PCP adds an IV and D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, for confirmed low sugar, keeps glucagon for when there's no IV, and transports after the first dose.
slides.sayZh: 很多中毒病人到你面前时意识水平下降、原因不明。在 BC，糖尿病急症流程也涵盖原因不明的意识下降，所以它是你的安全网。所有级别都要：用体位、吸引和气道辅助装置管理气道；给氧使血氧达到九十四以上；必要时侧卧；测生命体征，包括血糖，并检查卒中征象。血糖低于四点零、病人能保护气道，就给口服葡萄糖；EMR 级别如果病人不能保护气道，就给胰高血糖素。PCP 多了：开静脉，对确认的低血糖给 D10W 十到二十五克；胰高血糖素留到开不了静脉时用；给完第一剂就转运。

slides.q: A 45-year-old is found drowsy at home beside several empty pill bottles. He moans to pain, breathes 14 times a minute with good depth, and SpO₂ is 96%. BGL is 2.6 mmol/L. As the PCP, what comes next?
options: Put oral glucose gel in his mouth
Start an IV and give D10W 10–25 g, then transport
Give naloxone 0.4 mg and wait to see if he wakes
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A forty-five-year-old is found drowsy at home beside several empty pill bottles. He moans to pain, breathes fourteen times a minute with good depth, and his saturation is ninety-six percent. His glucose is two point six. As the PCP, what comes next? A, put oral glucose gel in his mouth. B, start an IV and give D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, then transport. C, give activated charcoal by mouth. D, give naloxone point four milligrams and wait to see if he wakes. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一名四十五岁男性在家中被发现嗜睡，旁边有几个空药瓶。他对疼痛有呻吟，呼吸每分钟十四次、深度好，血氧九十六。血糖二点六。作为 PCP，下一步是什么？A 把口服葡萄糖凝胶放进他嘴里；B 开静脉，给 D10W 十到二十五克，然后转运；C 口服活性炭；D 给纳洛酮零点四毫克，等着看他会不会醒。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. He has a decreased LOC and a confirmed glucose under four point zero, so the PCP starts an IV, gives D10W ten to twenty-five grams, and transports. Oral glucose, A, is only for patients who can protect their own airway, and he only moans to pain. Activated charcoal, C, is not in BC EMR or PCP scope, and it's dangerous in a drowsy patient who may aspirate. Naloxone, D, is for a suspected opioid overdose with depressed breathing; his breathing is adequate, and the low sugar is the clear problem now.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。他意识下降、血糖确认低于四点零，所以 PCP 开静脉、给 D10W 十到二十五克，然后转运。A 口服葡萄糖只给能自己保护气道的病人，而他只对疼痛有呻吟。C 活性炭不在 BC EMR 和 PCP 范围内，而且对可能误吸的嗜睡病人很危险。D 纳洛酮用于疑似阿片过量且呼吸受抑制的病人；他呼吸足够，眼下明确的问题是低血糖。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Stable now ≠ stable later: absorption continues
  • Expect vomiting at any time; suction ready
  • Recheck BGL and LOC after every intervention
  • An alcohol smell can hide a head injury or other cause
  • Count the pills; bring all containers to the ED
  • Never delay transport to collect vomit or pills
slides.say: Here are the new watch-outs at PCP level. A poisoned patient who looks stable now may not be stable in twenty minutes, because the body keeps absorbing the poison. So reassess often, and recheck the glucose and the level of consciousness after every intervention. Expect vomiting at any moment, and keep suction ready. Don't let the smell of alcohol end your thinking; a drunk patient can also have a head injury, low sugar or another drug on board. Count the pills and bring every container to the emergency department. But don't hold a sick patient on scene to collect vomit or pills. Transport comes first.
slides.sayZh: PCP 级别的新注意事项：现在看着稳定的中毒病人，二十分钟后未必稳定，因为身体还在继续吸收毒物。所以要勤复评，每次处置后都重测血糖和意识水平。随时可能呕吐，吸引器要备好。别让酒味终止你的思考：喝醉的病人也可能有颅脑损伤、低血糖或者还用了别的药。数一数药片，把所有容器带到急诊。但不要为了收集呕吐物或药片把重病人留在现场，转运优先。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Not in BC EMR/PCP scope: activated charcoal, atropine, pralidoxime, benzodiazepines, IO
  • Low sugar: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L at every age; IV dextrose = D10W only
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV q 3 min, or 4 mg IN; ventilate first
  • EMRs have no IV access in BC
  • No separate poisoning protocol in the BC exam guidelines
slides.say: Now the BC rules for this chapter. The textbook mentions several treatments that are not in BC EMR or PCP scope: activated charcoal, atropine, pralidoxime, benzodiazepines, and intraosseous access. Low blood sugar has one BC threshold, under four point zero, at every age, and the only IV dextrose is D10W. Naloxone in BC is point four milligrams, then point four, then point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, three minutes apart if needed, or four milligrams intranasal, and you ventilate first. EMRs have no IV access. And there's no separate poisoning protocol in the BC exam guidelines, so you build your care from protocols like the diabetic and narcotic overdose protocols.
slides.sayZh: 现在看本章的 BC 规则。教材提到的好几种处理不在 BC EMR 和 PCP 范围内：活性炭、阿托品、解磷定、苯二氮卓类和骨髓腔通路。低血糖在 BC 只有一个阈值：低于四点零，各年龄一致，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。BC 的纳洛酮是零点四毫克，再零点四、再零点八、再两毫克，IM 或 IV，需要时每三分钟一次，或者鼻内四毫克，而且先通气。EMR 没有静脉通路权限。BC 考试指南里没有单独的中毒流程，所以你要用糖尿病流程、阿片过量流程等来组合处理。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Route and scene first: several sick people, no mechanism = possible toxic gas
  2. Toxidromes: pupils, skin, breathing and pulse point to the drug class
  3. Unknown cause + decreased LOC: check BGL; PCP gives D10W for confirmed < 4.0

Next: alcohol, stimulants, sedatives and opioids, with naloxone
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: think about the route and the scene first. Several sick people in one place with no mechanism means a possible toxic gas, and you don't go in unprotected. Two: use toxidromes. Pupils, skin, breathing and pulse point you to a drug class, and the six history questions fill in the rest. Three: for a decreased level of consciousness with no known cause, always check the glucose; as a PCP you start an IV and give D10W for a confirmed level under four point zero. Next lesson: alcohol, stimulants, sedatives and opioids, including the BC naloxone protocol. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，先想途径和现场：同一地点多人生病又没有受伤机制，就可能是有毒气体，没有防护不要进去。二，用中毒综合征：瞳孔、皮肤、呼吸和脉搏指向药物类别，六个病史问题补全其余信息。三，原因不明的意识下降一定要测血糖；作为 PCP，确认低于四点零就开静脉给 D10W。下节课讲酒精、兴奋剂、镇静药和阿片类，包括 BC 的纳洛酮流程。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
